title: S2 scaffolding: rso/slice001 package skeleton, deterministic CI command, contract.json validator
objective: Create the stdlib package skeleton rso/slice001/ with a deterministic test entry point and a validator for contract.json shape, so every S2 packet has a place to put code and one command to run.
problem: S2 packets need a package, a test layout and one deterministic command whose output is a run record (counts of tests run/passed/failed/errored, start/end UTC, git SHA, dirty flag, wall and CPU seconds). The command is `python -B -m rso.slice001.ci` and runs unittest discovery over rso/slice001/tests with -B (no bytecode). It also validates rso/slice001/contract/contract.json against a JSON shape check (required top-level keys only: version, frozen, claim, world, reset_model, receipt, render, authority_stages, custody, gates, cases, challenge, caps, files) when the file exists, and reports ABSENT otherwise. No semantics: the checker verifies presence and types, not meaning.
non_goals: No scientific semantics: if a check would need to know what a gate means, escalate (rso-builder-role s5; Eupalamus charter)
Python >= 3.8 standard library only; no package installation (MWO-0004 R2)
evidence_required: a test that fails before the skeleton exists (RED) and passes after (GREEN)
a test that the CI command reports a deliberately failing test as FAILED with non-zero exit (cheat control: the runner can observe failure)
a test that a contract.json missing a required key is reported

acceptance.condition: exit 0 on the skeleton; the cheat-control test proves a failing test yields non-zero exit
